title: Deterministic Traffic Replay Benchmark for Private/VPC Customer Environments
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Build a deterministic traffic-replay benchmarking harness tailored for Private/VPC/on-prem customer environments. The harness must be able to ingest captured request traces (tokenized inputs, temperature/topk settings, streaming vs non-streaming), reproduce KV cache warm states, and replay traffic with deterministic scheduling so we can measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and other SLO curves in a way that is reproducible across local dev, dedicated clusters, and customer VPCs. Results must integrate with our regression detector (golden baseline comparison + automated alerts) and output artifacts consumable by Console dashboards and CI jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Trace format spec (JSONL) documented and validated against 3 sample customer captures
Replayer can seed KV/prefix cache state from a snapshot and verify determinism across 3 runs (<= 1% variance on tokens/sec and <= 5% variance on p95)
Supports network shaping (latency/jitter/bandwidth) via netem profile applied during replay
Generates a standardized metrics bundle: tokens_per_sec, p50/p95/p99, error_rate, gpu_util, memory_footprint
CI integration: benchmark step that fails when p95 regresses > configurable delta from baseline
Artifacts stored to S3/MinIO and Console dashboard ingest pipeline accepts new bundle format
tasks: Design trace format and capture tooling (token ids, model config, KV seed)
Implement deterministic scheduler in replayer (single-threaded deterministic timing mode)
Add KV seed/load hooks to runtime test endpoints
Integrate netem-based network shaping into runner container
Implement metrics exporter and bundle writer
Add regression comparator and CI gating step
Create runbook + Confluence doc with replay examples for solutions engineers
